finding.claim: Missing authorization on tenant wipe: wipe() calls requireRole(), which only returns a boolean and never throws, and discards the result. Any authenticated user, with or without the OWNER role, can trigger the destructive wipe of any tenant. export() uses checkRole(), which throws, so the two endpoints are inconsistent.
finding.source: Any authenticated caller of POST /tenants/{t}/wipe, who supplies the User and the tenant path parameter. No OWNER role is needed.
finding.sink: repo.wipe(tenant) at src/Admin.java:27, a destructive wipe of tenant data

trace.note: The Javadoc on requireRole states it returns true or false and does not throw.
requireRole returns u.roles().contains(role) and enforces nothing.
wipe() calls requireRole(u, "OWNER") as a bare statement, so the boolean result is discarded.
By contrast, export() calls checkRole, which throws SecurityException at lines 19-21 when the role is missing.

finding.guards_checked: The only guard on the path is the requireRole call at line 26, which has no effect because its result is ignored. There is no other check in the file. The file has no tenant-membership check either, though the User record carries no tenant information. checkRole in export() is correct. I found no other callers, tests, or middleware in the repo, since src/Admin.java is the only file.

verdict.guard_found: requireRole at src/Admin.java:14 returns a boolean and never throws. wipe() at line 26 discards the result. checkRole (lines 18-22) throws, but only export() calls it (line 32).
verdict.reason: src/Admin.java:26 calls requireRole as a bare statement, so its boolean result (line 15) is discarded and repo.wipe(tenant) at line 27 runs for any caller, whereas export() at line 32 uses the throwing checkRole.
